The receive window is lwIP's default (four segments of 536 bytes), so a stream moves about 2 KB per round trip; its limits are not the stream link's yet. The cross build with tcp for thumbv7m and thumbv7em against the cross-test port is still not run; Zephyr's port keeps LWIP_TCP at 0.
changes_bullets: lwip-sys: shim.c and wrapper.h gain wz_lwip_tcp_sndbuf and wz_lwip_tcp_window under LWIP_TCP, allowlisted in build.rs. wz-link-lwip: Cargo feature tcp (forwards lwip-sys/tcp), module tcp with LwipTcpSocket over a receive ring (connect, connect_in with TcpSocketPool, send_parts, try_read, shutdown, state, readable), TcpError and TcpState, and six tests against an echo server on the same stack: a frame in two parts, a ring that wraps with short reads (in lockstep), the peer's close read as the end, a connect to a port nobody listens on, a buffer below the window, and a write larger than the send buffer. scripts/lib/feature_public_surface_census.py names tcp in both wz-link-lwip rows.
Round 4216.decision_summary: The third step of the stream link for a node with no heap: one TCP connection of lwIP's raw API as a byte stream a cooperative loop can write to and read from without blocking (wz-link-lwip, feature tcp, LwipTcpSocket). Its state is address-stable storage lwIP's callbacks write into, a heap box or with static-link-storage a cell of a static pool (TcpSocketPool), written in place because it holds the receive buffer. The receive buffer is the flow control: a byte is acknowledged and the window reopened when the application reads it, so a buffer at least the port's window (read from the port through a shim, TCP_WND) holds anything that can arrive, and a smaller one is refused at connect. A write queues all its parts or none; a part lwIP then fails to queue would leave half a frame in a stream, so the connection is aborted and the call says so. The shim reads two lwIP macros Rust cannot reach, the send buffer left and the window.
verification_bullets: On a build host: the six tcp tests of wz-link-lwip pass (0.01 s), and clippy with warnings denied is clean with tcp and with tcp plus static-link-storage. The feature surface census, the prose-name gate, the armed-oracle census and wz_config --check pass. Two earlier runs of the same tests did not finish: the wrap test waited without a bound for echoed bytes the server had dropped, and both runs were cancelled after hours; the test now sends in lockstep and every wait is bounded. The feature gate diagnostic was not re-run (wz-link-lwip is off its axis) and the cross build of lwip-sys with tcp for the MCU targets is still not run; Layer Q is not re-run because the images do not set the feature.

carry_forward_bullets: The stream runs over the engine's StreamDriver with its own framing, a third copy of the frame cut beside the host's window and the node's new one in wz-session-core (stream_window); the driver should take the window in its place, with a fixed carry. Nothing hosts a TCP session yet: the slot host takes one driver type per table, so a node that dials tcp/ and udp/ needs the closed driver enum, and the dialer's locator parse and the links trait must accept tcp/ where they say Unsupported; there is no capability link-tcp for the node with its Kconfig, no listener (a node dials only), and no probe of a node holding a session with a stock router over tcp/ for 2000 requests and reconnecting. The receive window is lwIP's default, about 2 KB per round trip. The MCU cross build with tcp and the static-link-storage run of the stream tests are not done, nor Layer Q.
changes_bullets: lwip-sys: shim.c, wrapper.h and build.rs gain wz_lwip_now_ms (the port's sys_now) and, under LWIP_TCP, wz_lwip_tcp_local_port. wz-link-lwip: LwipLink::now_ms and LwipTcpSocket::local_port. wz-session-lwip: Cargo feature tcp (forwards wz-link-lwip/tcp) and module stream with LwipTcpStream (a StreamSocket: write and wait poll lwIP up to five seconds, a read polls once, shutdown sends the FIN) and LwipTcpDial (a StreamDial over a heap connection, or with static-link-storage over a cell of a TcpSocketPool), and four tests on the loopback against an echo server: a stream that writes, waits and reads like a socket (a wait with nothing coming ends at its time), the peer's close read as the end, a dial to a port nobody listens on refused, and the engine's StreamDriver framing a 300-byte batch over lwIP and handing it back whole. scripts/lib/feature_public_surface_census.py names tcp in the three wz-session-lwip rows.
Round 4217.decision_summary: The fourth step of the stream link for a node with no heap: the stream link the cooperative engine already has, written once for every stack with sockets, now runs over lwIP. The engine's StreamSocket and StreamDial are blocking contracts (a write returns when the stack has taken every byte, a wait when bytes are queued or the time is out), and lwIP here runs NO_SYS on the one thread that drives the session, so nothing moves in it until it is polled. LwipTcpStream and LwipTcpDial therefore make each wait a loop that polls lwIP, its input path and its timers (the acknowledgements and retransmission that move a connection), until the thing waited for has happened or the time is out. The time is the port's own millisecond clock, read through a shim, so the host and a deploy each keep their own definition. A dial returns when the handshake completes and is refused on a reset or after five seconds; a table without room is Exhausted, and a receive buffer below the window is Unsupported.
verification_bullets: On a build host: the four stream tests of wz-session-lwip pass (0.12 s) and the six tcp tests of wz-link-lwip still pass; clippy with warnings denied is clean for wz-session-lwip with tcp, and with tcp plus static-link-storage. The feature surface census and the prose-name gate pass. Not run: the cross build of lwip-sys with tcp for thumbv7m and thumbv7em (still, since the system stopped it for memory), the static-link-storage form of the tests (it is compiled and linted, not run: the tests use a heap box and the engine's heap transmit store), and Layer Q (the images set no tcp feature, and the new shim function wz_lwip_now_ms is not referenced by them, so the linker drops it; a footprint row that moves says otherwise).

carry_forward_bullets: This corrects the carry of the stream link round that put LwipTcpStream over the engine's driver: the driver should NOT take the window in its place, the two designs stay and the test holds them to one rule. The rest of that carry stands: the closed driver enum for a host mixing UDP and TCP, the dialer's tcp/ locator and the links trait where they answer Unsupported, the link-tcp capability with its Kconfig, a listener, the probe against a stock router, and the MCU cross build with tcp.
changes_bullets: wz-runtime-coop stream_link tests: every_chunking_of_a_wire_frames_the_way_the_shared_window_does feeds the same wire to a StreamDriver over a scripted stream and to a window over a fixed carry in all 171 ways of three reads, asserts the batches equal and that the population is the full count.
Round 4218.decision_summary: The stream link of the cooperative engine cuts a stream into batches in its own buffer, in place, while wz-session-core now holds a window that cuts the bytes a reader was handed. The first carry of the stream link said the driver should take the window in its place. That was wrong: the driver reads into the tail of one linear buffer and lends each batch where it lies, with no second buffer and no copy, which is the design a node with little memory wants, and the window would add a carry and a copy. So the two stay two designs for two kinds of reader, and the rule they share is held by a test instead: however the stream is cut into reads (every pair of cuts of a wire carrying a plain batch, an empty one, a one-byte one and a longer one), the driver and the window hand over the same batches, and both pass the empty batch over.
verification_bullets: On a build host: the twelve stream_link tests of wz-runtime-coop pass with session-unicast and alloc (the new one among them) and clippy with warnings denied is clean for the crate with those features. The fixed-memory form of the driver was not run.

carry_forward_bullets: Stage seven of the C ABI node: what is left answers Z_EUNAVAILABLE on a node: the advanced publisher and subscriber and their matching and liveliness, the group, shared memory, the info peers and routers, the transport and link events, the declared key expressions, the timestamp, the snapshot and the limits that read the registry. A witness of the publisher's and the querier's interest where it matters: a node below a router, with the subscriber beyond the router (control: the matching stays false without the interest). A querier's background matching listener has no test. Read the hosted run of the nondefault-features leg. The rest of the carry stands: a get with a cancellation token on a node answers Z_EUNAVAILABLE, a put or a query value of shared memory goes out as bytes on a node, a C ABI router that keeps no south is the registry of faces, router-node has no Kconfig switch or footprint budget, a client told no router that keeps a south is refused, and the dialled-subregion cases have no stock zenohd witness.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-capi-c/src/matching.rs: MatchTarget over the registry or the node, MatchingHold and the owned listener hold it, watch_on_node and next_interest_id, and the node arms of the status and listener doors of a publisher and a querier. crates/wz-capi-c/src/publisher.rs: NodePublisher holds the node, declares and withdraws an interest, keeps the background matching hold; publisher_state and not_a_registry_publisher are removed. crates/wz-capi-c/src/querier.rs: NodeQuerier likewise (interest, matching hold, plane); querier_state and not_a_registry_querier are removed; the background listener of a querier has its node arm. crates/wz-capi-c/tests/session_roles.rs: the matching test, and the two tests that said the matching was unavailable no longer say it.
Round 4219.decision_summary: Item 751 step (b), the C ABI holds a node, stage six: the matching of publishers and queriers. A publisher or a querier declared on a node now reports what matches its key. The node's publisher and querier hold the node counted (NodePublisher and NodeQuerier keep an Arc of RouterState in place of the data plane alone) and declare an interest on its data plane, which the node's router answers with the declarations beyond it, and withdraw it when they drop. z_publisher_get_matching_status and z_querier_get_matching_status read RouterState::matching_status (the subscribers for a publisher, the queryables for a querier, only the complete ones when its target is ALL_COMPLETE, as the registry's reads them); the owned and the background matching listeners of a publisher and the owned one of a querier are watches of the node's own face (RouterState::watch_matching), ended by the listener's drop. What a matching listener is declared on is now one type, MatchTarget, the registry's MatchId or the node's watch with the node counted, held by the background hold and by the owned listener alike. The accessors that answered Z_EUNAVAILABLE for these operations have no reader left and are removed. The test has a registry peer hold a subscriber and a queryable on a key and requires the node's publisher and querier on that key to say that something matches, by status and by owned and background listener, and a node publisher on a key nothing subscribes to to say it does not; it fails, each alone, with the publisher's status always false, the querier's status always false, the publisher's owned listener, the querier's owned listener and the publisher's background listener handed nothing.
verification_bullets: wz-capi-c with router-node: the library tests (185) and session_roles (13 of 13) pass on the final files, the new matching test among them. Controls, each alone and restored: with the node publisher's status always false the test fails on that status never saying the peer's subscriber matches; likewise for the node querier's status; with the owned listener of the node's publisher, the owned listener of the node's querier and the background listener of the node's publisher each handed nothing, the test fails on that listener never being told. A control that left the node publisher without its interest declaration PASSED: in this test the peer dials the node directly, so the node holds the peer's declarations whatever it asked, and the interest is not witnessed here; it is the node's behaviour in the Rust API and the topology where it matters (a subscriber beyond a router) is not tested. The querier's interest has no control of its own. Clippy -D warnings with all targets is clean for wz-capi-c and wz-capi-core in the default build, for wz-capi-c with router-node, and with router-node and zenoh-c-no-unstable-api. A first run failed on a field read only by its drop, repaired. Not run: the default-build tests after this change, the other wz-capi-c tests, the background listener of a querier on a node (it has the same body as the owned one and no test of its own), the advanced publisher's matching, the footprint and size gates, Layer Z, Z8.

carry_forward_bullets: The listener has no close: it is a static that listens for the life of the image, and closing it (clearing the accept callback, closing the block, dropping what waits) is for the first image that stops listening. The accepted connection reaches no session yet: the adapter that makes it a StreamListen of the engine's stream link, the slot stack that dials and accepts tcp/ in a host, the link-tcp capability with its Kconfig, and the probe of a node against a stock router are the steps after. The refusal is lwIP's abandon, without a reset of its own; how soon the dialler learns of it was observed to vary and is not asserted. The MCU cross build with tcp is still not run.
changes_bullets: lwip-sys: shim.c, wrapper.h and build.rs gain wz_lwip_tcp_remote_ip and wz_lwip_tcp_remote_port under LWIP_TCP. wz-link-lwip tcp: TcpError gains AlreadyListening and ListenFailed; LwipTcpSocket gains peer and the private adopt and boxed_inner (connect now builds its state through the latter); LwipTcpListener<RX, Q, S> (new const, listen or listen_in a pool, accept, waiting, refused, local_port) with its accept callback; two tests: the connection that arrived is handed out and reads and writes with the dialler as its peer (and a second listen is refused), and a full queue refuses the next connection, counts it, and ends the dialler failed while the first still waits.
Round 4220.decision_summary: The fifth step of the stream link for a node with no heap: the accept side. A node listens on a port and takes the connections that arrive on it, each handed out as the same LwipTcpSocket a dial yields, so a session over a connection is the same whichever end opened it. The listener is a static the image declares, as the datagram listener is, with a queue of Q connections waiting to be taken. A connection that arrives with no room for it, because the queue is full or on static-link-storage every cell of the pool is taken, is refused in the accept callback: lwIP abandons it, nothing is allocated instead and the refusal is counted. The connection is registered in the accept callback itself, before lwIP goes on to the data of the same segment, so nothing a peer sent with its handshake is missed. A shim reads the other end's address and port, so an accepted socket knows its peer, which a dialled one learned from its own call.
verification_bullets: On a build host: the eight tcp tests of wz-link-lwip pass (the six of before and the two new), and clippy with warnings denied is clean with tcp and with tcp plus static-link-storage (compiled and linted; the tests use a heap box and are not built under static-link-storage). The first run of the refusal test failed on an assumption about when lwIP tells a refused dialler (it waited for an established state that came or did not, as lwIP chose); the test now asserts only that the dialler ends failed. Not run: the cross build with tcp for thumbv7m and thumbv7em, Layer Q and the feature gates (no feature was added).

carry_forward_bullets: Nothing yet opens a session over a connection: the slot stack that dials and accepts tcp/ in a host (the engine's IpStack takes a DatagramSocket for udp/, and lwIP's UDP is not one, so the stack here is lwIP's own, with a driver that is a closed choice of the datagram driver and the stream driver), the dialler's locator and the links trait where they answer Unsupported, the link-tcp capability with its Kconfig, a listener close, and the probe of a node against a stock router stay open. The MCU cross build with tcp is still not run.
changes_bullets: wz-session-lwip stream: LwipTcpListen<L, RX, Q, S> (new over a link handle and the static LwipTcpListener; StreamListen with local, the port it listens on, and accept, which polls lwIP and yields an LwipTcpStream whose peer the socket reports), and the test a_dialled_and_an_accepted_stream_carry_batches_both_ways_through_the_stream_link.
Round 4221.decision_summary: The sixth step of the stream link for a node with no heap: the accept side meets the engine. LwipTcpListen is the engine's StreamListen over the static listener of the link tier, so a node takes the connections that arrive on its port as the same LwipTcpStream a dial yields, and the stream link over a connection has nothing to tell which end opened it. Each accept polls lwIP once, because a connection arrives as its handshake is processed, and wraps the oldest waiting connection with its peer read from the socket. One test holds the whole path together: a dialled end and an accepted end, each under the engine's stream driver, carry a 300-byte batch one way and a 500-byte batch the other, whole, with the accepted end knowing the dialler's port.
verification_bullets: On a build host: the five stream tests of wz-session-lwip pass (the four of before and the new one), and clippy with warnings denied is clean with tcp and with tcp plus static-link-storage. No feature was added. Not run: the cross build with tcp for thumbv7m and thumbv7em, Layer Q, and the static-link-storage form of the tests.

Then stage seven: the advanced publisher and subscriber and their matching and liveliness, the group, shared memory, the info peers and routers, the transport and link events, the declared key expressions, the timestamp, the snapshot and the limits that read the registry. changes_bullets: crates/wz-capi-core/src/drive/router_node/local_face.rs: Command::CancelQuery and LocalLiveliness::cancel_query. crates/wz-capi-core/src/drive/router_node.rs: RouterState::get_numbered and cancel_get; get is get_numbered without the id. crates/wz-capi-c/src/get.rs: issue_get_on_node takes the node counted and the token, and registers and records the cancellation. crates/wz-capi-c/src/liveliness.rs: the liveliness get on a node registers the token for the snapshot. crates/wz-capi-c/tests/session_roles.rs: the cancellation test.
Round 4222.decision_summary: Item 751 step (b), the C ABI node: the first of the carried debts, the cancellation token of a get. A get on a node is now ended by the token it was made with, and a liveliness get on a node takes the token as a registry's does. The node's own face learns to end a query it holds: a new command CancelQuery(rid) delivers the one final the held query waits for (LocalLiveliness::cancel_query), RouterState gets get_numbered, which answers the request id the query was asked under, and cancel_get(id), which ends it; RouterState::get keeps its signature. issue_get_on_node registers the token's fan before it asks, as a registry's get does (a token whose cancel has started fails the get with Z_EGENERIC), and records, after the id is known, the undo that cancels the query on the node; a token cancelled while the query was being asked runs the undo there and then. The cancel of the token waits for the registrations to be released, which the face does as it lets go of the query's handlers, so the closure's drop(context) has run when the cancel returns. A liveliness get on a node takes its snapshot on the face's thread before it returns, so there is no leg to stop; the token is registered for its length and one whose cancel has begun fails it with Z_EGENERIC. The refusals by name (Z_EUNAVAILABLE) that stage four and five left for a token are gone. The test has a registry peer's queryable hold a query for four seconds, the node's get be made with a token, and the cancel return at once with the get's closure let go; it fails with the cancellation not registered (the cancel then waits the query out, 3.95 s).
verification_bullets: wz-capi-c with router-node: the library tests (185) and session_roles (14 of 14) pass on the final files, the new cancellation test among them. Control, restored: with the cancellation not recorded the test fails on the cancel waiting for the query to run out (3.95 s against a limit of 2 s); one run of that control ended at the bx reservation (exit 137) and was rerun, which is not a code verdict. Clippy -D warnings with all targets is clean for wz-capi-c and wz-capi-core in the default build, for wz-capi-c with router-node and with router-node and zenoh-c-no-unstable-api, and for wz-capi-core with router-node. Not run: a liveliness get with a cancelled token on a node (the code fails it with Z_EGENERIC; no test reaches it), a cancel of the token of a get that was made by a querier of a node (it takes the same path), the default-build tests after this change, the other wz-capi-c tests, the wz-zenoh tests over RouterState::get (its signature is unchanged and it compiles in the router-node build only through the C ABI here), the footprint and size gates, Layer Z, Z8.

carry_forward_bullets: No session runs over the stack yet: the stack is exercised through its drivers, and a handshake and a Put over it need the slot host built over LwipTcpStack (its tables, runtime and entropy), which the exhaustion tests of the UDP host show the shape of. The node that listens and dials (the admin node of the slot profile) is typed to the UDP driver and is not made generic; a node of tcp/ links is built from the generic session host and the connect manager until it is. Mixing udp/ and tcp/ in one host needs lwIP's UDP to be the engine's datagram socket, or a closed driver of the two; neither is done. The link-tcp capability with its Kconfig, a listener close, the probe against a stock router and the MCU cross build remain.
changes_bullets: wz-runtime-coop: DatagramSocket gains CARRIED (default true), udp_link gains NoDatagram (no value, CARRIED false), and the udp/ arm of IpStack::bind_initiator and of the heap links' dial answers Unsupported when the datagram socket is not carried. wz-session-lwip stream: the alias LwipTcpStack (IpStack over NoDatagram and LwipTcpDial, under session-slot) and the test a_tcp_only_slot_stack_dials_and_accepts_tcp_and_refuses_udp_as_unsupported (tables empty after the refusal, both links hold a receive buffer, a batch of 400 and a batch of 700 cross each way); the two stream tests that build heap drivers are off the slot profile.
Round 4223.decision_summary: The seventh step of the stream link for a node with no heap: the pieces meet the engine's slot stack. The engine already has IpStack, one stack for udp/, tcp/ and tls/ links that claims each link's buffers from the image's byte tables and yields the one driver type the session host runs, with an acceptor for the connections of a listener. It was written over a datagram socket the platform provides, which lwIP's UDP is not, so a node of tcp/ links names a datagram socket that does not exist: NoDatagram, as the stream side has NoStream and NoDial, with a DatagramSocket::CARRIED constant the stack asks before it claims anything. A udp/ dial on such a node is then Unsupported and permanent, never an Exhausted that is retried. LwipTcpStack is that stack over lwIP's dial. A test dials and accepts through it, shows the udp/ dial refused with every table still empty, and carries a batch each way between the two drivers.
verification_bullets: On a build host: the four stream tests of wz-session-lwip pass with tcp and session-slot (the slot stack test among them), the five with tcp alone, and the 57 lib tests of wz-runtime-coop pass with session-unicast and alloc. Clippy with warnings denied is clean for wz-session-lwip and wz-runtime-coop with tcp, session-slot and session-unicast-accept, and for wz-session-lwip with tcp. Not run: the cross build with tcp for thumbv7m and thumbv7em, Layer Q, and the static-link-storage form of the tests.

carry_forward_bullets: The carried debts of the C ABI node that remain, in order: the meaning of a C ABI router that keeps no south (it is the registry of faces, which forwards nothing), the Kconfig switch and footprint budget of router-node, and the stock zenohd witness of a node that dials into a south. The value of a get in shared memory goes out as bytes on a node (RouterState::get has no descriptor path, as the Rust API's node has none). Then stage seven: the advanced publisher and subscriber and their matching and liveliness, the group, shared memory's provider on a node (z_obtain_shm_provider answers Z_EUNAVAILABLE), the info peers and routers, the transport and link events, the declared key expressions, the timestamp, the snapshot and the limits that read the registry. A witness of the interest of a node's publisher and querier where it matters (a node below a router) is still owed. Read the hosted run of the nondefault-features leg.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-capi-c/src/put.rs: node_publish_payload, and the node arm of z_put uses it. crates/wz-capi-c/src/publisher.rs: the node arm of z_publisher_put uses it. crates/wz-capi-c/src/bytes.rs: Outbound::bytes is no longer built for router-node, which implies queryable. crates/wz-capi-c/tests/session_roles.rs: the shared-memory put test (built with router-node and zenoh-c-shared-memory).
Round 4224.decision_summary: Item 751 step (b), the C ABI node: the second of the carried debts, the payload of a put in shared memory. A put (z_put and z_publisher_put) made on a node with a payload that is a chunk of shared memory now goes out as the chunk: RouterState::publish_shm with the chunk's send handle, which the node sends as its descriptor to a face that negotiated shared memory and as its bytes to any other, as the registry's put does. node_publish_payload is the one place a node's put decides which of the two a payload is. The value of a query is not carried the same way: RouterState::get takes bytes and has no descriptor path, the Rust API's node asks with the bytes as well, so a get on a node sends a chunk-valued query as its bytes and that stays. The test puts a chunk through a node to a registry peer that dials it and requires the peer's subscriber to be handed the payload as a chunk of shared memory (z_bytes_as_loaned_shm answers Z_OK); the same test run before the change reached the peer and failed on its being the bytes of the put, so the two are a pair.
verification_bullets: wz-capi-c with router-node and zenoh-c-shared-memory: session_roles passes 15 of 15, the new shared-memory put test among them. Control: the same test run before the change (the node put the chunk as its bytes) reached the peer and failed on the peer being handed the bytes of the put and not the chunk of shared memory; the change is what turns it. Without the shared-memory feature, router-node: the library tests (185) and session_roles pass (the shared-memory test is not built there). Clippy -D warnings with all targets is clean for wz-capi-c and wz-capi-core in the default build, for wz-capi-c with router-node, with router-node and zenoh-c-shared-memory, and with router-node and zenoh-c-no-unstable-api. Not run: z_publisher_put with a chunk through a node (it shares the function, no test of its own), a node put of a chunk to a face that negotiated no shared memory (the bytes leg of publish_shm, which the runtime owns), the library tests in the shared-memory build, the other wz-capi-c tests, the footprint and size gates, Layer Z, Z8.

carry_forward_bullets: The test does not carry data: a Put over the session, and the router that a node reaches over tcp/ in practice, are the next measures; the probe against a stock router for 2000 requests with a reconnect is the done condition of the stream link and is not run. The admin node of the slot profile is typed to the UDP driver, so a node that listens, dials by a configured endpoint and reports is not yet buildable over tcp/ from that node; it is built from the generic host and the connect manager. The link-tcp capability with its Kconfig, a listener close, the mix of udp/ and tcp/ in one host and the MCU cross build remain.
changes_bullets: wz-session-lwip: the integration test session_over_tcp (registered in Cargo.toml with the features of the slot profile, tcp and the close encoder): a runtime cell, two session tables with their pumps, the byte tables of each node's stack, a static TCP listener; the dialling node opens its link through its stack's bind_initiator inside the host's dial, the accepting node takes the connection through the stack's acceptor and opens it on its host; the loop turns until both ends are established, then the dialler closes and the acceptor's task finishes.
Round 4225.decision_summary: The eighth step of the stream link for a node with no heap, and the first that runs a session over it: one node dials a tcp/ endpoint and another takes the connection off its listener, each on the session host of the fixed-memory profile over the stack of the step before, and the handshake runs through lwIP's TCP, the engine's stream link and the slot tables. Both ends reach the established state, the dialling link takes a receive buffer and a frame buffer from the image's tables and the accepted one a receive buffer from its own, and when the dialler closes the acceptor's session ends. The two nodes share one program, one lwIP stack and one cooperative thread, as the UDP exhaustion tests run theirs; what the test holds is that the pieces fit, which the drivers' own tests could not say. No source changed: the stack, the dial, the listener and the host were enough as they were.

Round 4227.decision_summary: Item 751 step (b), the C ABI node: the third of the carried debts, the meaning of a C ABI router. In a build with router-node a router opened through the C ABI is now the router data plane whatever it holds, where it was the registry of faces unless it kept a south apart, and the registry joins none of the faces it holds, so a router that was one forwarded nothing between its clients; mode "router" asks for a router, and a router that forwards nothing is a preset that does not do what upstream's does. OpenPlan::node_role names the node a role is opened as for a surface that opens every router as one (a router always, a peer or a client by node_for_south, as before) and the C ABI's open reads it; the Rust API opened every router as the node already. A peer or a client that keeps no south apart is still the registry of faces in the C ABI, which is the same question for a peer that listens and is left as it was. A build without router-node is unchanged: its router is the registry of faces, which forwards nothing, and that is now written in the carry. The test has a router and two clients that dial it and cannot reach each other, and requires what one puts to reach the other's subscriber, which only a router that forwards delivers; run against the open as it was before this change it failed on the put never reaching the other client, so the change turns it. The older routers tests of the file still pass, a router that listens on nothing hears its own put.

The tests of the other files that mention a router and need no zenohd pass with router-node: gossip_introduces (5) and open_refusals (1); client_only_dials_a_listener runs no test in that build and is no evidence. Clippy -D warnings with all targets is clean for wz-capi-c and wz-capi-core in the default build and with router-node, and for wz-capi-c with router-node and zenoh-c-no-unstable-api. Round 4228.decision_summary: Where the stream link of a node with no heap stands before the switch that selects it. The engine's admin node, AcceptingAdminNode, is already stack-neutral: it takes the host, a binder, an acceptor of the links a peer opened and the factory, and the Zephyr secure-channel admin node is that node. A node of tcp/ links over lwIP is therefore that node over the stack of the earlier step and needs no node code, only a Copy stack, because the node holds it as its host's and a copy as its binder. LwipTcpDial, and so LwipTcpStack, are Copy when the link handle is. The capability link-tcp and its Kconfig are NOT declared in this round, for two reasons: the MCU's Kconfig axes belong to the zephyr-admin-node image, whose lwIP backend builds only the UDP node, so an option would select nothing that builds (and the declaration declares no option that cannot be built); and on the host the tcp/ link is in every build, so a switch needs the tcp code gated and every combination built.

Round 4233.decision_summary:
The reds of hosted run 41788035479 are repaid, each in the place its gate named, plus one new red the lwIP tcp work on main would have raised next.

C1co and C1st (AwaitRelease never constructed): AwaitRelease and its impls are built only with `advanced`, which holds its only holders; the client-only and reduced C ABI builds carried it unused.

Qzk (zephyr-admin-fixed-tls, hosted only): the stack bound counted call sites on rows addr2line answers with line 0. The hosted runner's object files name those rows after the codegen unit, the workstation's after the source file, so a rule matching by file counted differently on the two machines. A call on a line-0 row is now placed at the nearest earlier instruction of its function that has a line. The pins follow that placement: admin-text-out 15 and json-text-out 11.

C1cn (lwIP TCP tests claimed by no leg): lwIP's TCP tests could not be given a leg as they were, because under `static-link-storage` they did not build; they called the heap profile's connect and listen. The tests now reach both profiles through wz-link-lwip's test_bind binders (tcp_connect, tcp_listen), and each profile has a leg for lwip-sys, wz-link-lwip and wz-session-lwip. listen_in now refuses a second listen before it takes the pool, so a refused call changes nothing.

The tcp/ slot-profile tests that main gained since (session_over_tcp, admin_node_over_tcp, the slot stack in stream.rs) did not build under `--all-features` and no leg ran them. Their root was in wz-link-lwip: TcpInner was not Send, so a TcpSocketPool was not Sync and could not be the `static` its own constructor's doc names as its use. TcpInner is Send by the same cooperative single-thread rule the datagram socket's Inner states. With that in place, each node of those tests declares its connection cells as an image does and the tests run on both profiles, each profile with its own leg. The session that owns those tests was told before the repair.

C1bzr (reduced-configuration docs): the stream_window module docs named their targets by short names, which rustdoc resolved under no feature set of the crate (all features included). They now name them from the crate root, as pool_gauge's do. GroupLivelinessSubscriber exists only where a multicast session, its only maker, does (transport-multicast). Round 4235.decision_summary: A defect found reading the code for the board image, in the stream the earlier steps built: its blocking waits (a dial's handshake, a write's wait for send-buffer room, a read, an accept) poll lwIP's loopback queue and timers, and an Ethernet interface's frames reach lwIP only when its MAC is polled, which is the image's. The host tests ran over the loopback, which lwIP moves by itself, and passed; on a board the SYN-ACK of a dial arrives through the MAC, so every dial would have waited its five seconds and been refused. The image now says what else a poll does with a Service, a plain function so the dial, the listener adapter, the stream and the stack stay Copy, and each poll runs it first, as the node's own loop pumps its ports before lwIP's timers. A dial or listener given none polls as before. A test counts the service across a dial, a wait and a read.

Round 4258.decision_summary: Item 751 step (b), the C ABI node, stage seven: what the faces of a node say. The peers and routers a session is linked to (z_info_peers_zid, z_info_routers_zid), the transports and links it lists (z_info_transports, z_info_links) and the listeners that hear of a transport or a link coming and going (the declared and background forms of both) now answer on a node from the node's own face table, where they read the registry's sessions. One value carries it, FaceSource (SessionHandle::face_source): the registry's SharedSession or the node's RouterState, answering the faces it holds, the observer that watches their coming and going and the undoing of it, so a listener keeps its own copy and unwatches after the session handle is gone. The node answers from RouterForwarder::face_snapshots and watch_faces, which the Rust API's node reads the same way, so no core change was needed. A node joins no multicast group through this ABI, so its transports are its unicast faces. The resource snapshot stays unavailable on a node on purpose: it counts the messages a session received, a node counts none, and a snapshot of zero would read as a node that received nothing.

Round 4264.decision_summary: The runtime task tables of the fixed-memory node images hold one cell per session, not one more. The tables were declared SESSIONS + 1 "with room beside" the pump tasks, but a node spawns no task besides a session's pump (the only spawn on the slot path is spawn_pump), and a session's cell is held until its handles are let go, which is the moment the session's slot is freed, so the cells in use never outnumber the slots in use. session_pool_exhaustion holds this at the host: it fills the tables to exactly N sessions (the task table of 2N + 1 cells is exactly full at the N + 1th session) and readmits a peer into the cell a closed session freed. Round 4265.decision_summary: Item 751 step (b), the C ABI node, stage seven: the advanced publisher. The composite (AdvancedPublisherOn, in wz-ext-pubsub) was hosted only on the registry through CPlane, so ze_declare_advanced_publisher answered Z_EUNAVAILABLE on a node. The composite is generic over a plane, so a node gets a plane of its own, NodePlane: the cache queryable is hosted on the node's data plane (host_queryable_from, retracted by unhost_queryable on drop), the @adv liveliness token is the node's own token (declare_token and undeclare_token), a put is the node's publication (publish_with, or publish_shm for a chunk), the heartbeat period is a thread that ends when its timer is dropped, and the entity id comes from a process-wide counter. The clock is the node's: RouterForwarder::node_hlc hands out the node's shared NodeHlc (a second clock with the node's identity would break the uniqueness of its stamps), so a node whose role does not stamp refuses a cache with no miss detection with Z_EGENERIC, as upstream's does. The state of an advanced publisher in advanced.rs became a host (the registry's shared session with its composite, or a node with its composite and the interest it declared on the node's data plane so that a node below a router learns of the subscribers beyond it), and the matching of an advanced publisher (listener, status) reads the host. The registry arm is the code it was, moved under the host. What stays unavailable on a node: the advanced subscriber and its matching and liveliness, the group, the resource snapshot.

Round 4266.decision_summary: Round 4259 bound a declared node's commanders to the verbs, and a consumer could still not write a grant to a declared node: a node with a secure channel made its key when it started, so its zid was known only once it ran, while a grant is compiled into the node that holds it. The key is taken only when its owner alone may read it, its text is wiped once the channel holds it, and a node that cannot be the identity it was told stops rather than make another. The zid it proves is known before it runs: `wz_node.py --zid-of` prints it from the certificate, by the rule the vocabulary states, so no consumer writes the rule again. Running the two nodes found that the declared node's reply line was cut at the console's 256 bytes, so a reply past about a hundred bytes was reported as other bytes than the node kept; the line is now written whole.

Round 4273.decision_summary: Item 751 step (b), the C ABI node, stage seven: the advanced subscriber. Its host (EngineSubscriber, in wz-ext-pubsub) is written over the port's SessionEngine and nothing else, and ze_declare_advanced_subscriber read the registry, so a node answered Z_EUNAVAILABLE. A node is now an engine: RouterState implements SessionEngine (a new file in wz-capi-core, drive/router_node/engine.rs), each operation being the one the node's data plane already does for the program that holds it. A subscriber is hosted on the data plane (one callback, where a registry mints one for each face), a liveliness subscriber is the node's own face's, a queryable is hosted with the node's holder, a token is the node's token, a get is the node's own face asking (one leg, whose callback is let go at the query's end, with its cancellation recorded on the fan), matching reads the node's tables, and the faces are the forwarder's; subscribers and liveliness subscribers share the one id space the port states, held by a map. Periodic jobs (the history's and the recovery's periods, the beacon's) run on PeriodicJob, a thread that ticks until it is dropped or its tick says stop; the advanced publisher's heartbeat of the previous round moved onto it, so there is one such job and not two. What a node does not do is stated in the file: a write filter holds nothing back (the router forwards by what the faces declared), the declared keys are none (a node names every key whole on the wire), the batch windows are zenoh-pico's, and the liveliness get is not offered through the engine yet. The state of an advanced subscriber in advanced.rs holds a host (the registry's shared session or the node), which the detection of publishers reads to declare its liveliness subscriber on the node's face, and the node's liveliness field in RouterState became counted, so that the cancellation of a query can hold the face on its own. What stays unavailable on a node: the group and the resource snapshot.

Round 4278.decision_summary: Item 751 step (b), the C ABI node, stage seven: the group. Unlike the advanced subscriber, the runtime's group (wz-runtime-tokio group.rs) was not written over the port's engine: it is bound to a unicast Session and to tokio tasks, and the C ABI joins one such group for each face the registry holds and takes their union in the aggregate (GroupAggregate). A node is one data plane, not a session, so the owner chose to lift the shared core and not to write a second group: what the two hosts share is now wz-session-core's group_view (the keys, the ids that may join and in what order they are refused, the keep-alive period, GroupEvent, MemberTable and react, which apply an event to the table of known members with their lease deadlines and say what the host must do: tell the user, or ask the member for its record). It is written over plain values with no lock, no clock and no channel, so it is no_std and the runtime's group and the node's both run it. The runtime's Group was moved onto it (its ten tests pass as before; the view of known peers is ordered by member id now, where it was in a hash map's order). A node joins ONE copy over its engine (NodeGroup in wz-capi-core, group/node.rs): the join is announced on the event key before the event subscriber is declared, the subscriber and the member's queryable are hosted on the data plane, the keep-alive and the watchdog are the engine's periodic jobs (no tokio runtime is asked for, which the registry's join needs entered), and a member heard of by its beacon alone is asked for its record by a query of the node's own face, every answer kept; its events go into the same aggregate under one source, so the view, the leader, the events and the wait are the C program's as before. wz_capi_c_group_join reads the handle and holds either host (GroupHost) and leaves it when dropped, the sink retired first as the registry's leave does. A group id or member id that may not join is Z_EINVAL on a node as on the registry, and a refused declaration Z_EGENERIC. What stays unavailable on a node: the resource snapshot.

Round 4282.decision_summary: The multicast session's task (multicast_pump_task, the group node's pump) is written as the session's task is: a function that returns an async block and not an async fn, and spawned with the future made in its cell. As an async fn it held each by-value argument twice in its future, once as given and once as the local its body moved it into (the reason pump_task is a block), and its callbacks carry the node's state (the group's observer, the publisher's schedule); and spawn_multicast_pump built the future by value on the caller's stack before the spawn. The future of the group's task no longer holds those copies, and the spawn no longer needs a frame as large as the future. The function's callbacks are closures, so their types cannot be named from outside the group's join and the cell of the group's task cannot yet be derived as the session's is (cell_bytes_of takes a function of two arguments, and the group's task takes four, three of them closures); that is the next step, not this one.

Round 4291.decision_summary: The structural remedy for the size of a test build is measured and its tools are in. Each of the 584 `tests/*.rs` files of the crates is a test executable of its own that links the whole dependency tree: one feature set of `wz-integration-tests` (317 files, default features only) is 71.3 GB of target on a build host, 318 executables of 217 MB each with the line tables only, and Layer C1bnl's 99 legs took 90 GB of a build machine's disk. Three facts the measurement found and the tool now holds: `zenoh_pico_sys` (the vendored C library) and `wz_capi_pico` (its drop-in) define the same `z_*` symbols, so one executable cannot link both and a file that uses one goes to a target of its own (`it_<crate>`); a file that installs a `#[global_allocator]` or has a `[[test]]` table stays its own executable (35 and the tables of six crates); and a file that runs its own binary by test name (`current_exe` with `--exact`) must name the test by its module path, which two files of this crate now do by `module_path!()` so that the name is right in both layouts. The move itself is not in this round: more than twenty gates read `crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/*.rs` by path and `run-ci.sh` names the files 230 times by `--test`, so the move carries them, and this round holds back until they can see both layouts. Round 4294.decision_summary: A declared node's identity can now be made on the device it runs on. The node binary takes `--make-identity <certificate> <private_key>`: it generates a P-256 key in PSA with export allowed, signs a self-signed certificate over it, and writes the key (SEC1 DER armoured as PEM, created 0600 with O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW and fsynced) before the certificate beside it, then prints the certificate's PEM on stdout. Nothing is ever overwritten: when both files are there it reads them as the node would and prints the certificate that is there; when only one is there it makes nothing and says so, so that a key is never paired with a certificate that is not its own; a certificate that fails to write takes its key back. The key's DER and PEM are wiped once written. The vocabulary's identity entry names the command and states that it never overwrites, and the zenohd interop test now provisions both nodes with the node's own maker instead of the external tool, holding that the printed certificate equals the file, that the key is 0600, that a second run changes nothing, that half an identity is refused, and that each node proves the zid --zid-of names for its certificate.

Round 4297.decision_summary: Phase 2 of docs/router-table-snapshots.md: a route memo keeps the newest inputs it has served. A route is a function of the graph and the interest table, kept by the versions of both (RouteInputs) and served only at the inputs it was computed at. Until now a store or a refresh at any other inputs cleared the memo; once readers hold different versions of the tables at once (structure B), a reader of an older version would clear what a reader of a newer one stored, a loss of work and never of correctness. RouteInputs::precedes orders inputs: both members are counters a write of the tables moves forward and nothing moves back, living as long as the hat that owns the memo (verified: the tables and their memos are constructed together, and the counters are sums of Versioned counters). A store from inputs that precede the kept ones returns its route and keeps nothing; a refresh to them moves nothing and asks the table nothing, decided under the read lock. A pair where neither precedes the other (a wrapped counter) replaces the memo, as every move did before, so the cache cannot be held back by an unordered pair. Under structure A inputs never go back, so nothing changes there.

Round 4303.decision_summary: Phase 3 of docs/router-table-snapshots.md: the router's tables are Clone by path copying at field granularity, so that the snapshot cell of phase 4 can publish a new version by copying only what a write reaches. Each hat's graph and interest tables, each face's routing facts, and the keyed stores beside them sit behind an Arc, and a writer reaches each through a named accessor that calls Arc::make_mut, which copies only when another version shares the component. The route memos are shared by every version and never copied (phase 2 made that sound), and each face's runtime stays shared as phase 1 left it. The recompute flag of a mesh hat and the record of the tokens advertised into each region lose their locks: every write of both was traced to a writer of the tables (the methods that write the record now take &mut self under T: DerefMut, so a reader cannot reach them by type), and the record sits behind an Arc like the other stores. Nothing clones the tables yet outside a test, so under structure A every Arc has one owner, make_mut never copies, and no behaviour moves.

Round 4304.decision_summary:
Two hosted reds are repaid at their root. The nightly Fuzz run (42016507903, at b0caa2b649) failed its `selector_term` job on an input from the `pcap` corpus. The soundness oracle offered the term `Push.del.timestamp.zid == 617320737570726f63205d393420205b` and found it Unknown over the very record whose tree held the field (rule S1). The input was a `Frame` whose `Push` carried a `Del` with a timestamp of a twenty-byte zid. The generated timestamp codec refuses that zid (`sce:max-size="16"`), and so do zenoh-pico and zenoh. The dissection walker read any VLE length, and every reader of a zid field reads at most sixteen bytes, so the zid printed as a value that did not name its own bytes. The walker now refuses a zid past sixteen bytes in `SpanCursor::zid`, the one constructor every zid site goes through. Two of those seven sites take a VLE count (the timestamp and the linkstate entry); the other five take a four-bit nibble and could not exceed it. The refusal is the codec's own `LengthOutOfRange`, and the dissection's serde name table now names it, so a persisted dissection records it by its name and not as "Unrecognised".

CI run 42011089802 (at 0c7298a48d) failed Layer C1cn: clippy `large_enum_variant` on `wz-zenoh`'s `Engine`. Its `Router` variant was at least 352 bytes, against 104 for `Tokio`, once the router node took an ABI extension and an engine state of its own (8ef208ab60, ed4d766806). The variant is now `Box<RouterEngine>`. A node is opened once, so one allocation keeps every peer and client session at its own size. The session that owns the router mode of `wz-zenoh` was told before the fix.

The same run's other two reds were attributed rather than repaired here. The bare-`.output()` census red in `validate + verify + test` was already repaid by 3522f080a1. The C1cs red is the eight cases that round 4290 and 9e3e643439 moved. That run predates both, and its hosted readings all fall under the moved budgets: pico-client 1,892,417 against 1,906,600, pico-default 4,470,378 against 4,499,900, capic-default 9,606,825 against 9,642,000. Round 4311.decision_summary: Phase 4 of docs/router-table-snapshots.md: the router's tables can be shared as published snapshots, value `snapshot` of the new choice policy `routing-table-sharing`, beside `rwlock`, upstream's reader-writer lock, which stays the default and the value of every upstream preset. One cell (router_forward/tables_cell.rs) holds the tables in either form behind the seam the router already had (OnTables over a read or a write). Under `snapshot` a reader loads the last published version from an ArcSwap and pins it for its thread, so that every nested read of that thread routes by the version its outermost read loaded, as a thread's reads see one state under the lock; a writer takes the writers' mutex, drafts the next version as a path copy of the published one (phase 3), and WrittenTables::drop, the one commit point, publishes the draft with one store before letting the mutex go, or abandons it when the write unwound. The guarantee that nothing is sent to a face after it left is held under `snapshot` by a grace period: deregister, after its write is published and the mutex released, waits until no reader holds a version retired before it, and a thread that holds a version and asks for a grace period is refused by an assertion, since it would wait for itself. The multicast ingress now owes its callbacks to the end of the route as the unicast paths do, under both values, so a callback of the node's own subscriber may declare while the group's ingress routes to it. The draft is allocated as the Arc it is published as, so a publish moves nothing. What `snapshot` gives up is stated in the policy's help: a message routed under the version before a change may reach a link after a declaration that change sends to the same link, which no rule of the protocol orders. Nothing here says what either value costs; phase 5 measures both against the baseline of round 4286. The same land counts the router tests of phases 2 to 4 in the CI lanes that pin them (C1AY, C1X), whose counts phases 2 and 3 had left behind.

Round 4314.decision_summary: The steps for what only a stream suffers (a connection that ends by FIN or by RST, one that falls silent, a listener that stops, a message the network cuts or joins, a peer that comes back) are designed by the property a stream link owes and built on an instrument that makes the network do each, and the instrument is the first piece. scripts/lib/stream_fault.py is a TCP proxy with one control for each thing a network does (close_all, reset_all, blackhole, refuse, segment, and hold with flush), and it is deterministic by construction: a counter is raised before the bytes it counts are sent, every thread waits on events (select and a wake pipe) and none decides by a timer, the thread that owns a resource carries a control out and acknowledges it so a control returns when its effect is in place and the connections the kernel had established before it are taken first, segmentation is judged by the writes the proxy made and a merge is an explicit barrier, an orderly release is the half-close protocol so unread data never turns it into a RST, and the cases wait on a signalled state and never sleep and look. A first version of the same proxy flaked in 3 runs of 30, from a counter raised after the send and from a close that raced the thread using the socket; the design above is what removed those causes and not a longer wait. HARDWARE_VERDICT.md states the properties, the rules the steps follow (a fault on one leg observed through another, bounds from the node's contract and not from a run, a step that waits for a state and not for time) and the reference-model discipline the steps are accepted by.
verification_bullets: The proxy's selftest holds each control to its effect as the ends see it, against a real echo server on the loopback (EOF with no reset for an orderly release even with 20,000 bytes in flight, a reset for an abortive one, silence with nothing forwarded and the bytes counted dropped for a black hole, a refused connect and a held connection that still works for a closed listener, the proxy's own write log for segmentation, one write for a hold released by a flush). It passes 300 runs in one process, and 100 runs beside 64 busy processes on a 32 core machine, with no failure; the earlier version failed 3 of 30 and, before that, 4 of 6. The selftest bites: with the count made after the send it fails three cases at once, and with an abortive release made orderly it fails the case that holds it. gate_provenance_lint, round_fed_gate_reach, the board table gate and the verdict program's selftest pass, bash -n and shellcheck are clean. Not built yet: the steps themselves, their reference model and its faults, and the run of any of them against the node under QEMU or on the kit; this round is the instrument and the design.

Round 4315.decision_summary: Item 751 step (b), the C ABI node: router-node is ON in the default build of the C ABI (wz-capi-c) and of the core (wz-capi-core). The owner asked for the structure that is right for the long term, textbook and ultimate, cost set aside, and this is the answer. Reasoning. wz is an extensible framework and zenoh, zenoh-c and zenoh-pico are presets of it; the parity of a preset is that preset's contract and a PARTIAL atom is a debt. The default feature set of the C ABI is the zenoh-c preset, and zenoh-c opens a router in its default build, so a default build that opened a registry of faces that forwards nothing was the stated gap that `upstream_on` set against `default = "off"` in deploy/wz-config.toml. The declaration is the single place the answer lives: the `default = "off"` line is removed (a capability with no `default` is on), the generated Kconfig and the two upstream defconfigs follow (zenoh-c_defconfig and zenoh_defconfig no longer need the line, since it is the default), and the manifests of the core and of the C ABI list it in their default, which `wz_config.py --check` holds equal to the declaration. A build that leaves the node out (a client, a small peer) says so: host-client-tcp-query keeps CONFIG_WZ_CAP_ROUTER_NODE=n. The cost is the owner's figure and it is paid knowingly: 1,285,904 bytes of text (13.3 percent) of the default build, with no export of its own (836 in both builds). So that a build without the node keeps being graded and does not become free to grow, the cost gate gets a case for it: capic-default now holds the node (its budget is the reading and the 3,184 the hosted lane reads over this machine and 3,500, to the hundred, 10,927,900) and capic-default-lean is the same features without router-node, forbidding its symbols, at the budget capic-default had (9,642,000). Two checks that depended on the old default are corrected: the census of feature-only tests (the three SKIPS rows of the zenohd interop module advanced_and_group named tests that `--all-features` never lists, since the module is cfg(not(zenoh-c-no-unstable-api)); the rows fail as tests that no longer exist and are dropped, the module being run by Layer Z all the same) and the census of public-surface features (router-node and the routing-namespace it implies are no longer non-default features of wz-capi-core, so they leave the waiting list, as the node-config features did in R3418). The document of the C ABI's node says on instead of off.

The phase 0 instrument, four runs each: under snapshot a declaration takes 516 to 566 us at the median where rwlock's took the 10 ms bound (10 025 to 10 029 us), a face transition 72 to 83 us against 10 028 to 10 056 us, and one writer completes about eighteen times the writes; the readers route 12 to 14 per cent fewer Puts a second (1.09 to 1.11 M against 1.24 to 1.27 M) while that writer publishes eighteen times as often. Layer E7s, one pair: per message snapshot costs 2 to 6 per cent more, within the spread E7s has shown on one host; the three tests that wait for 2 048 sessions to come up on a starved router fail under snapshot (1 735 and 1 700 came up within the deadline) and pass under rwlock. The cause is the copy each write pays: every face that comes up is a write, and every write copies the face map's spine and each store it reaches, so n faces cost O(n squared) on a core with little to give. The verdict recorded in section 6.2: snapshot as built is not a value a deployment should choose; rwlock stays the default; phase 6 (profile what a write copies, make those tables persistent, and remove the outermost read's per-message count if the profile shows it) comes before any recommendation, and B is recommended only when a reading of it holds every E7s test and costs no more per message.

Round 4324.decision_summary: The first steps for what only a stream suffers are built: HW.36 (an orderly release by the peer ends that peer's session and no other, at once), HW.37 (an abortive release: the same) and HW.38 (conservation and re-establishment: after more releases than the node has cells the node still takes its peer back and holds one session for it). A step is a stimulus, an observation on the other leg and a comparison that is a pure function of what was observed. The comparison is the only thing that decides: the wait runs to a hang guard and measures, and judge_release and judge_conservation judge, so weakening a comparison goes green and no second term holds the step red. The bounds come from the node's contract and not from a run: the lease the node advertises, the keep-alives in it, the retry schedule of a dial and the cells of its pool, held equal to the node's source by a drift check that names the constant that moved. Prompt means below the earliest moment a lease could have expired (the lease less one keep-alive interval, three quarters of it), so a node that waits out its lease fails. The acceptance of the steps is a reference model of the contract on a virtual clock with a fault for each way a node breaks a property: each model fault reds exactly the step that holds its property and no other. A first real run against the node under QEMU read the node's own console as 2, 1, 2 sessions three times while the program saw no release: a router redialling at once passes the one-session state before the next read. A state that holds is the observation, so each release now closes the leg to new connections before the fault (the counter before the effect) and opens it after the read, and the model implements the refusal.
verification_bullets: The model's selftest: a node that keeps its contract holds all three steps with 7 of 7 returns; each of six faults (a cell lost on a reset, a cell lost on an orderly close, a FIN noticed only when the lease runs out, a RST noticed only then, an accept that sticks after the first release, a release that also ends the other session) reds exactly the steps that hold its property, with HW.37 not run where the release before it left no peer to release; the two comparisons weakened let their faults go green; a fixture that was never established fails every step by name; moving the lease, the retry ceiling, the keep-alives per lease, the cells or the sessions in the program's copy reds the drift check each time. The verdict program's selftest passes with the base output unchanged and the new cases: the steps run after HW.0 to HW.7 through the program, every printed sentence is an instance of the grammar, each model fault reds its steps, a failed base step leaves the stream steps printed and not run, an environment with no proxy is refused by name, and a udp node or a pool image beside the option is refused. A second proxy sits on the leg the node dials B over, the node is told to dial it, and the proxy stamps every connection it takes on its own clock before it does anything with it, so the gaps between the node's dials are events. Round 4330.decision_summary: The admission property of a stream link is the seventh step of the stream suite: HW.42, a peer past the node's capacity does not harm the sessions it holds, and the node takes its peer back once it has gone. The step now judges that: it stands five idle connections straight at the listener (not through the proxy, which would stall its own accept loop on a listener that drops what it cannot take), waits as events for the node to close the ones it cannot hold, and requires that at most the capacity of two still stood at two seconds, which is below the reap, so a refusal is told from a reaping. While they stand a query through A (a held session carrying a request and its reply) must be answered with both sessions and B must still report both; closing them must give their cells back, which one release of A and its return show. The capacity is derived from the contract, the accepts constant joins the drift check, and the step's comparison is one pure function with four model faults: a session taken down to make room, a cell kept after the connection is gone, a pressure that never lands and a node that holds every connection.

Round 4333.decision_summary: Coalescing is the other half of framing and the ninth step of the stream suite: HW.44, several requests that arrive in one read are each answered whole, and the node's sessions are as they were. HW.41 cuts one message into many reads; this joins many messages into one. The leg to A is held (the proxy buffers what router A sends the node and forwards nothing), eight requests are made through router A together, and the buffer is then sent as one write. Eight is more than one and few enough to fit the node's batch at 128 bytes each. The barrier that shows every request arrived is the buffer's content and neither a size nor a time: each request carries a tag of its own in its selector, which router A passes on as it is, and the wait is for every tag to be in what the proxy buffered, on the proxy's condition and to a guard below the lease, so the keep-alives that also cross the held leg cannot stand in for a request (a byte count would have let them). The proxy's hold was reworked for it: the state is per connection and per direction under that direction's lock, and a release ends the hold and sends the buffer in one step, so a read landing between the two is neither sent ahead of the buffer nor stranded in it, and it returns the writes that call made, so a write made by a later read cannot be taken for the buffer's. The log of what was buffered is kept as it was read. The comparison is one pure function (requests made, every tag buffered, exactly one write, every answer both sessions, both sessions held afterwards); five model faults each red it alone (a tail of the read dropped, a wrong reply, requests never handed over together, a request that never reached the buffer, a session reset after right answers), and each comparison weakened to drop one clause lets its fault go green. The batch joins the drift check, for the one node that states it as a constant. The step is not run when HW.42 did not hold.

Round 4336.decision_summary: Phase 6 of docs/router-table-snapshots.md (section 6.3). A second instrument times the writes of an admission by band of faces already up and the copy of each store: on the tree of phase 5 a write under snapshot at 2048 faces cost 2.5 times rwlock's for a subscription (1313 against 521 us) and 4.6 times for an interest (602 against 130 us), almost all of it whole copies of the future-subscription store and the broker hat's client subscriptions (191 to 398 us each). Those stores are now persistent maps (a hash array mapped trie written for the router, Bagwell 2001) whose writers read first and write only what changes; after it, at 2048 faces, 968 against 935 us and 256 against 227 us, every store's copy 0 us but the face map's 10 us. The starved router's bring-up still failed, and a bring-up timeline showed why: every session that came up did so in the first 10 s (the accept timeout) and none after, under rwlock as well (2048, 1451, 1350 of 2048 against snapshot's 1773, 1056, 1324 as the host's load went from 2 to 9), because the harness started the router on one core at nice 10 instead of moving it there once its sessions were in, as its own comment said. With the harness corrected, E7s passed every test in two alternating runs of each value at host loads of 3 to 30, per message within the spread of either value; with no writer the instrument's readers route within 2.6 per cent of rwlock's, so the outermost read keeps its count. Snapshot is the recommended value for a router whose sessions come and go; the default stays rwlock, as C2 requires of every policy.

Round 4341.decision_summary: A board row's verdict_steps names the steps its record was made against, and it could name one step or one range. A stream node's steps are not one range: HW.0 to HW.7 are every node's, HW.8 to HW.25 are the second interface's, HW.26 to HW.35 are the datagram pools', and HW.36 to HW.44 are what only a stream suffers, so the row of the node over tcp/ could not name what it has run without naming steps its image does not carry. The scope is now one or more step expressions joined by ' and ', each a step or a range, in ascending order without overlap: the order and the no-overlap are what give a scope a single spelling, so the witness's verdict text can be held to the same words as before (the first step expression it opens with must be the scope itself, so a record that names only the first range does not stand for a scope of two). Every step inside every range is still read as before: published by the grammar, named in the entry, OK and not FAIL. The narrowing remains a narrowing of what the record must name, and not a way round the grammar.

Round 4348.decision_summary: A querier of a lifecycle verb is declared by its words, not its key: verb, of (the zid of one of the node's peer endpoints), about (a zid or self), whatami (client unless stated), generation for reset, mode for open; one of key and verb. The generator makes the key as lifecycle_wire::VerbKey reads it, so no declaration and no consumer spells the key grammar, and raises the node's key budget to the longest key such a querier can ask. about = self is the node's own zid, a fact of the node when it runs (its [identity] or a key it makes at start), so the key is generated up to its last chunk and the node ends it at start through slot_querier::LaunchedKeys (written once before the node exists, read as the 'static key a Query asks). The node says each querier's key at start, HOST-WZ-QUERIER <n> <key>, so a consumer joins the ASKED, REPLY and VERDICT lines to the querier by its place in the declaration.

Round 4362.decision_summary: The datagram pool steps now run on the kit. The kit lane captured the console of the node under test and ran the program's board mode against it for the steps every node has, HW.0 to HW.7, and for a stream node the stream steps; the pool steps, HW.26 to HW.35, judged from the same console, the program's own output and a capture of the node's frames, were run by hand on the bench in round 3315 and by no lane since. The lane now starts a capture of the frames to and from the node's address at the host's wire before the reset, and for an image built with a pool (the table says which, as POOLS) it puts the run to that pool's steps once the program's output is written. Making that run stand on its own found two faults of the lane's reading, which are fixed because a lane that is right three times and wrong a fourth is not a verdict. First, the directory of a built image is the same for every run of it, so a file a run waits on (a READY line in the console, 'listening on' in the capture's output) was read from the run before when the wait came before the process that writes the file had truncated it; the first run of the pool image was judged on the previous boot's READY line, whose node id the node under test did not have, and the run's own steps failed on it. A run now removes the console, capture, reset and verdict files of the run before it before it does anything, and the boot under test is cut from the console at the first Zephyr banner after the reset, which is told by the console and not by a clock. Second, a capture is ended by a signal sudo hands to its command only once the command runs; a signal sent in the first moments after the start was taken by sudo and lost, and the lane waited on the capture for ever. The signal is now sent until the capture has gone, and a capture that cannot be ended is said to be.

Round 4364.decision_summary: Layer U asked two questions in one command. Its verdict on the tree is whether the pins agree with what upstream had published, and whether the workflow's cache keys and toolchain agree with the pins. Whether upstream has published since is a fact about the world, not about any commit. Because the lane called the releases API itself, one commit could be green one day and red the next, a machine without gh and a token could not judge it, and the fleet placed it nowhere. The fleet's owner recommended splitting it rather than handing the fleet a token. The API's answer is now an input the tree carries: scripts/lib/upstream_releases.json, written by `upstream_release_distance.py --fetch` where gh is authenticated, holding each derived repository's releases and each pinned ref's toolchain channel, with the sha256 of that body. Layer U reads only that file. Item 578's condition 3 holds on both sides. The verdict fails on a snapshot that is absent, does not match its digest, or is silent about a repository or pin the tree now names, so a pin bump refreshes the snapshot in the same commit. `--watch` compares the snapshot with the live API on a daily schedule (upstream-watch.yml), outside the check set, and fails when upstream has moved or cannot be read. The fleet's C0 run of this change then failed in the fault proxy's own stress cases, which run on every C0. Measured on a loaded build machine, two defects showed. A reject's reset can reach the client at its connect rather than its first read, and the case allowed only the read. The proxy's release ended the hold one direction at a time, so the reply to what it sent up landed in the still-held down direction and was returned as the buffer's own. The release now ends both directions and sends both buffers in one step under both locks.

Round 4367.decision_summary:
A Zephyr image can now state the policies it reads. Until this round the image's build passed the limits to cargo (WZ_LIMIT_*) and no policy, and its Kconfig tree did not hold Kconfig.policies, so a policy could be set in the host flow only. The declaration now says, per image, which policies the image's code reads ([[policy_image]], with an optional requires expression over the options of the image's axes and the global axes that holds a policy to the profiles that run its code). The generator writes the image's own Kconfig.policies from those rows and, in wz_axes.cmake, wz_axes_policy_env: WZ_POLICY_<NAME>=<value> for each policy whose value is not upstream's, which the image's CMake adds to the cargo environment where SessionPolicy reads it. An image's Kconfig does not source the host tree's file, which names every policy: --check holds that and holds that an image that reads policies sources its own.

The rows rest on the call path from the image's own sources, traced for each of the fourteen policies, not on the crates the image links. The Zephyr admin node reads three: tx-no-progress-deadline and tx-expiry-keeps-session in every profile (its session factory builds the transmit queue from the build's policy), and declaration-sync-pacing in the fixed-memory client only (the client node of the slot profile). The other policies are read by code the image does not run (the tokio runtime, the C ABIs, the node clock and event log, the supervisor, the router) or are an assertion of the build and no run-time read. A policy the image does not name is an undefined symbol in its tree, so Zephyr stops the configuration; one it names outside its profile is Zephyr's own warning that the assignment was not honoured, which Zephyr keeps as a warning by design.

Upstream's regions test waits for three peers of a router by counting the Put events (`wait_for_n_peers`); on router 73aa9301 it counted two peers and the same peer again, stopped waiting, and began publishing while a third peer (73aa9310) was linked to the other region-3 router only. Router 73aa9300 then read itself the only gateway of that peer and carried to it a sample that the publishing peer, in the same region, had already sent it directly: one subscriber saw the sample twice and `unique_timestamps` failed. Measured on the build fleet with the test repeated: before the change 6 to 18 failures in about 400 runs (1.5 to 4.4 percent, the rate recorded before the router table phases as well, so those phases were not the cause); after it 397 of 397 pass. The earlier readings of this residue as a window between two gateways' views of a peer's links (the 4121 barrier for a dialled second link) were right that the sample was carried twice and wrong about why the scenario reached that state; the barrier stays. An accept-path barrier written for that reading was measured against the failure (9 of 414 failed, unchanged) and was not kept. Each listener now keeps a ledger of what it was told up (`FaceLedger`, wz-capi-core): a face told up is not told up again, and a down is told only for a face told up, so the order of the watch and the history does not matter.
